content:
Just weeks after announcing a price increase for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also raising its prices. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the monthly fee for Apple TV will increase from $12.99 to $14.99.

The individual plan of Apple One is also raising its price.

Apple TV and Apple One price increases

Below are the details of the price increases:

  • Apple TV (monthly): $14.99 (originally $12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): $119 (originally $99)
  • Apple One Individual Plan: $21.95 (originally $19.95)

Other Apple One plan prices remain unchanged. Last month, when Apple raised the price of Apple Music, it also adjusted the Apple One Family Plan and Apple One Premier Plan, but did not raise the Individual Plan.

New pricing takes effect today for new subscribers. Apple stated that existing subscribers will receive a price increase notification about one month before being charged at the new price.

Apple last raised the price of Apple TV in August 2025, increasing the monthly fee from $9.99 to $12.99. At that time, Apple did not adjust the annual plan or the pricing of the Apple One bundle.

Over the past year, Apple has significantly expanded the content lineup of Apple TV. Last October, Apple announced that it had become the exclusive broadcast partner for F1 in the United States. F1 streaming is included in the standard Apple TV subscription fee, with no additional charge required.

Earlier this year, Apple also added the U.S. Major League Soccer streaming service to Apple TV, with no additional charge required. Previously, watching MLS required a separate subscription to MLS Season Pass.

Apple is also benefiting from the recent success of several productions, such as the fourth season of "Ted Lasso." Season 2 of "Dark Matter" premieres on Apple TV today. Season 6 of "Slow Horses" will premiere on September 16.

What are your thoughts on the new pricing of Apple TV? Is $14.99 reasonable for the content offered by Apple TV? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
